newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Telecel says part of stock to be floated in U.S..
newsitem.headline: Telecel says part of stock to be floated in U.S..

text.p: Portuguese mobile telephone company Telecel said that part of its proposed share flotation will be offered in New York.
Company officials declined to give further details.

Earlier, the company had said it would offer some 7.6 million shares, equal to 35.6 percent of its capital, on the market at between 6,900 and 8,100 escudos per share. The offer is expected to be completed in Lisbon by December 10.
There will also be a green shoe that would take the total potential stock on offer to 39 percent.
The proposal would value Telecel at between 148 and 174 billion escudos ($977 million to 1.15 billion).
The main shareholder in Telecel is Telepri, a holding jointly controlled by Banco Espirito Santo and the Amorim group, which has 75 percent.
The company expects some 66 percent of the offer to be sold directly to institutional investors with the remainder being offered as a public offer to sell (OPV) on the market.
